column3: Locked scales for 2D viewports (D27). A viewport quotes one of these; the Viewport Settings panel shows one toggle button per scale, finest first (1:20, 1:50, 1:100, 1:200 - the last added 21-Sep-2026, for a whole building or a street on one sheet). The fallback list in Na__LayoutEditor__ConfigState__SheetSetup__.js mirrors this one: a saved scale that is on neither list is coerced to DefaultScaleDenominator on load, so the two must agree. A site plan viewport quotes one of SitePlanScaleDenominators instead. THE SITE PLAN LIST IS THE ONLY ONE THAT COUNTS: SitePlanExportConfig.SupportedScaleDenominators in the Tags SSOT is documentation and is read by nothing. A denominator of 500 or finer is a BLOCK PLAN, which draws the full fill / pattern / linework composite; coarser than 500 is a LOCATION PLAN, which draws only the proposed fills, no hatch patterns, and greyscales every line that is not a boundary or a proposal. THE SCALE ONLY DECIDES A VIEWPORT THAT HAS NOT BEEN TOLD: Viewport__SitePlan.SitePlan__PlanType overrules it, so a large site CAN be drawn as a block plan at 1:1250 and keep its patterns. The rule itself lives in Na__LayoutEditor__SitePlanComposites__Config__.json, which is what the app reads; the sentence here is the note beside the scales it applies to.

column3: AccordionSections are the sections that behave as one group. column3: The Project Specification tab: every drawing note of the project, in groups. A group has a prefix (GN, SN, EE) and a title; a note has a title and its specification text. A note's code is its group's prefix and its place in the group, zero-padded to NumberDigits - GN01, EE02 - so moving a note up or down, moving it to another group or changing its group's prefix renumbers it. Specification bubbles on the sheets link to a note by its id, not its code, so a renumber reaches every bubble on every sheet. The specification is a file of its own (FileName) beside TrueVision__ProjectData__.json, kept locally in the project folder so an agent can edit it on disk, and written to the same R2 key on Sync. LegacyFileName is the previous R2 name, read only when FileName is not there yet. The file is read when the drawing editor opens. Every edit is kept in this browser at once (DraftEnabled, written DraftDebounceMs after the typing pauses); Sync writes the whole file to R2 and to the local copy, and first asks whether to replace a cloud copy that changed since it was read (ConfirmCloudOverwrite). HistorySteps is the tab's own undo depth.

column3: The notes margin a sheet can carry down its right-hand side, from the top of the border to the title block. Switched on per sheet with Show notes margin in the Margin Notes panel; drag its left edge to make it wider or narrower. It lists any groups the sheet lists without leaders first (LeaderlessNote), then the specification notes the sheet's bubbles link to, in specification order, then the general notes. Distances and text sizes are paper millimetres except the divider and rule (printed points). TextSizeMm is the body (2 mm); titles are TitleScale times that. PaddingMm is the left and top/foot inset; PaddingRightMm is the clearance before the sheet's right border, a little more so wrapped lines do not clip. A note reads as its code, CodePipe, then its title, with the body wrapped to the full inner width. A faint RuleColour line at RulePt sits between notes, centred in the gap between them: NoteGapMm is the least that gap can be, and decides what fits; when every note fits and the column has room left at the foot, every gap opens by the same amount, up to NoteGapMaxMm. IncludeGeneralNotes and GroupHeadings are what a newly switched-on margin starts with.
